positions.claim: The number of new drugs developed per year is declining despite advances in technology and AI, the inverse of Moore's law.
AI gains confined to the research and development stage of the drug pipeline will not meaningfully shorten the overall 10-year timeline; innovation is needed across the whole pipeline.
RNA-seq is the modality most used for single-cell foundation model training primarily because it is easier to measure and scale, not because it is the most biologically informative.
Proteomics would arguably be more valuable than transcriptomics because proteins do most of the functional work in the body, but it is too low-throughput to train on.
Two measurements of identical cells do not produce the same reading, making single-cell data intrinsically heterogeneous in a way text data is not.
Compressing single-cell data into a latent vector destroys information, which is why transformer-based single-cell models underperform.
Simple linear models sometimes match or outperform compute-expensive transformer-based single-cell foundation models.
Single-cell foundation models perform worse relative to their training cost than foundation models in language and imaging domains, a view the speaker says is shared in the community.
Flow-matching models currently outperform autoregressive and autoencoder-based models on single-cell data because they match the full distribution rather than predicting the mean.
Progress requires both massive data scaling and improved measurement quality; scaling existing low-quality data alone will not produce models that generalize to unseen data.
Quantum computing may eventually be a natural fit for the high-dimensional multi-state nature of single-cell data, but classical AI is what is available now.
